scene-u01-pnew1-65.text: Why single link is the minimum and complete link the maximum

scene-u01-pnew1-66.name: text#66
scene-u01-pnew1-66.text: $\tfrac12(a+b)-\tfrac12\lvert a-b\rvert=\min(a,b)$; switching the minus to plus gives the maximum. So single link takes the closest pair and complete link the farthest.

scene-u01-pnew2-83.name: text#83
scene-u01-pnew2-83.text: Misconception: is single link always worse?

scene-u01-pnew2-84.name: text#84
scene-u01-pnew2-84.text: No. When the data really are elongated chains, single link recovers them; no linkage is always best.
